messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need to pick one performance initiative to prioritize for the Q2 roadmap. Options (short):
  1) Tail latency (p95->p99 improvements for chat)
  2) Throughput (tokens/sec per GPU, batching improvements)
  3) Cost (unit token cost via quant + packing)

sanjay: Do you want us to use RICE or impact/effort?

zoe: I sketched a lightweight spreadsheet and impact buckets — link: https://docs.internal/redwood/perf-prio (TL;DR below)

derek: engineering POV: throughput wins for batchy inference, but a lot of our customer pain right now is tail latency for interactive chat. Latency needs KV cache + priority scheduler to be convincing.

li: low-effort wins exist: prefix KV caching + smaller batching tweaks. Medium impact, low effort. Could be quick win in 2 sprints.

maya: Important bit — top 3 customers asked explicitly for <150ms p95 for chat in sales calls. That pushes latency higher in urgency. Also need launch criteria and rollback plan.

sanjay: If we go hard on latency we may need pinning to smaller model variants or fast-fallback routes; that increases infra cost and operational complexity.

zoe: Quick RICE-ish sketch (back-of-envelope):
- Latency: Reach 0.6, Impact 7, Confidence 0.6, Effort 3 -> score ~ (0.6*7*0.6)/3 = 0.84
- Throughput: Reach 0.7, Impact 6, Confidence 0.7, Effort 4 -> ~0.735
- Cost: Reach 0.8, Impact 5, Confidence 0.65, Effort 2 -> ~1.3
(note: numbers fuzzy — used to compare order, not exact)

maya: So cost optimization looks attractive by RICE, but that risks quality regressions if quantization affects outputs. We need guardrails.

derek: Agree. Proposal: sequence work so cheap cost levers are behind flags + automatic quality regressions checks against our eval suite before rollout. Then tackle latency routing as a canary.

prod-bot: Deploy bot: Reminder — feature flag FF-321 (KV-cache) currently default=off in prod.

li: Proposed sequence (minimal scope):
- Sprint 1: prefix-KV cache rollout (small cohort) + batching micro-optimizations
- Sprint 2: quantization experiments behind FF + automated evals + dark launches
- Sprint 3: latency routing (priority lanes + fast-fallback) + canary on customer tier

maya: Launch acceptance criteria — need these explicit. Example minimal criteria:

zoe: ```
Acceptance criteria (example):
- p95 for chat route <= 150ms OR fallback success >= 99%
- no >2% relative degrade on eval prompt set (quality) after quantization
- autoscaler keeps 99.9% of requests within latency SLO during 10m ramp tests
- metrics surfaced in Console per-route (cost, p50/p95/p99)
```

derek: Rough engineering estimates: cache infra + rollout + infra changes ~2w, batching tweaks ~1w, quant infra + eval harness ~3w, routing + prioritization ~2w. Contingency + integration -> plan for 8–10w total but split across sprints.

li: Vote: +1 for the sequence (cache -> quant -> latency). :thumbsup:

sanjay: +1 from me. Also add sales comms item so customers know what to expect during canaries.

zoe: +1. I'll own the RICE spreadsheet and track actual impact after first rollout.

maya: OK locking plan. Action items:
- derek: post RFC in eng-runtime with perf baselines and detailed estimate by Mon.
- li: build quant eval harness + smoke tests.
- sanjay: coordinate customer comms and set expectation for canary window.
- zoe: update the prio sheet with these sequences and flags.

derek: Will do. Posting RFC and perf numbers Monday morning.

maya: Thanks everyone — I'll add this to roadmap doc and tag sales for the top customers. 

prod-bot: Note: this thread archived to #roadmap-tracking when Maya pinned the message.
